utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We had no time to discuss anything on 92 bis, but could I ask the Prosecution to indicate especially as far as the authentication witnesses are concerned, to indicate clearly what documents are in these piles of documents that were tendered and whether they were admitted or not and perhaps also to consider whether there would be any need to ask for 92 bis statements to be admitted into evidence if documents are admitted and if the Chamber did not ask for any authentication or if it is not challenged.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Until you added that last comment, Mr. President, my attitude have been that because of challenges that were made to the documents that were tendered it was to include the 92 bis authentication as well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But we would like to know exactly what documents they are about. So this is not an opening of the debate on 92 bis, but just in order to give the Prosecution some time -- some homework for the weekend. We will adjourn until next Monday, 9.00, same courtroom. And I thank especially the interpreters for their patience and their flexibility and cooperation on this late Friday evening and the same, of course, is true for the technical booth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 7.12 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 1st day of July, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25
